title: Korea: bad food and a narrow escape from K-5
summary: They play near the front; the camp they left is wiped out the next day.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: First we went to Tokyo, and we stayed there until we got our shots and so forth. Then we went to Taegu, and we stayed there for two or three days, and played for the bases there, all the different setups they had there. So we played for that. Then we went up North to Korea, which was horrible. Boy, they gave us some jive food that was halfway cooked, and everybody had diarrhea, so you know we had the shits all up and down in North Korea.
Yeah, at once. Everybody had to... They all

got sick. But we ate it anyway. We went on up to Mae West Hill and up where all the front-running troops were. Like, we were at one place, I think they called it K-5; that night we played for them, and we went back to the tent. Then the next morning we got up and got on the trucks, and we were heading back down to K-10, and the gooks come over the hill and wiped out K-5. We had stayed over that night. If they had come an hour earlier, they'd have got all of us. But anyway, we went down to the... After we got down there, we found out that the gooks had come over and wiped out everybody where we were.
Did you wear helmets and everything when you were traveling up near the front?
Yeah, we wore those, too. We wore helmets and everything -- except for the clothes. We didn't wore the... We wore the outfits, what they call fatigues...

Yeah, we wore those things. But that's about all. We had to do that in Korea because it was so filthy over there, man. The dirt was everywhere, man. We'd ride down in a jeep. We'd ride from one camp to another, and by the time we'd get to where we were going, dirt would be all over you...
